airflow.note: the cooling system provides front-to-back chassis cooling (Figure 38 for models without PoE).

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX2300 Switches: "The power supply in EX2300 switches is built in along the rear panel of the chassis"; Table 34 lists "Switch with built-in power supply"; the cooling system is "two fans built-in along the rear of the chassis" and the non-PoE rears (Figures 11 to 13) show a single exhaust opening. Nothing in the guide describes removing or replacing either. They are part of the chassis, not bays and not components.

chassis.note: Table 3: height 1.75 in (4.45 cm), width 17.4 in (44.19 cm) and 19 in (48.26 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 10.2 in (25.9 cm) for models without PoE capability, weight 8.28 lb (3.76 kg). 441.9 x 44.45 x 259.0 is carried: the metric as printed for width and depth and the height as the 1U pitch Table 35 gives (1.75 in, 4.45 cm). The photographs show no ears, and the jack pitch closing on the registry at that width says the figure is the body.

colour.note: median of the bare front plate in the 24P photograph (#919599); the plate at the top right #6e7276.

front-console.note: estimated - the mini-USB console port (guide Figure 4, callout 5, printed CON) is drawn as chassis art, a 7.9 x 4.6 mm shell with its opening, read off the 24P and 48P photographs (25 x 14 px and 24 x 14 px at 3.27 px per mm). It is not a component: the library has no mini-USB receptacle and its DCIM export has no row for one, so a placed part would export nothing. The rear RJ-45 console port is a component and exports.

front-layout.note: estimated - the 48-port front is the 48P photograph's without the PoE items: the guide says the PoE lamp is present only on models with PoE capability, so three port-mode lamps (SPD, DX, EN) and no POE legend, and the red PoE+ mark beside the model name is not drawn. No photograph of a non-PoE front exists, so the model name is printed EX2300 as on the PoE units. The 48 jacks stand in four shells of six columns, the first jack at 9.36 mm and the shell step 88.8 mm (6 x 13.97 plus a 5.0 gutter), so the last shell ends where the uplink block begins at 364.6; the rows are 14.8 mm apart and the upper row is turned 180 so its lamps and keyway are above, as the photograph shows. The four SFP+ cages abut on the registry pitch of 14.25 at 364.6, one row. A darker plate carries the model legend and lamps at the top right and runs down the far right edge. The hexagonal vent fields along the top edge and above the uplinks, and the slotted row along the bottom edge, are read off the same photographs. The flower mark beside JUNOS, a logo, is not drawn.

gate-1.note: The 48P front photograph is 1500 x 300 px with the body 1432 px across and about 142 down (the lower edge carries a shadow): 10.1 against the stated 441.9 / 44.45 = 9.94, so x is taken at 3.24 px per mm from the width and y at 3.19 px per mm from the height. The ganged jack pitch reads 13.96 mm, the 0.550 in pitch the registry records for the ganged RJ-45 cell, on a quantity the scale never saw. The 24P photograph agrees on every feature both show to within 0.7 mm in x and 1.4 mm in y; the y values here are the mean of the two. The 48P rear photograph reads 3.234 px per mm across and 3.09 down. Every position is estimated and good to about a millimetre.

lamps.note: Hardware guide, Tables 4 to 12 and Figures 24, 26 and 27. Each RJ-45 port and uplink has two lamps, Link/Activity and Status; Figure 24 puts Link/Activity on one corner of the jack and Status on the other. The Status lamp reads out whichever of SPD, DX and EN the Factory Reset/Mode button has selected (PoE too on a PoE model), shown by which port-mode lamp is lit. SYS is green, ALM red or yellow and MST green. The jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary because a block cannot override it per lamp. On the uplinks the left slot is taken as Link/Activity and the right as Status by analogy with the jacks, which no figure confirms, so it is estimated.

port-numbering.note: photo-measured - the photograph prints each column's two numbers in orange under the shell, the even number up and left and the odd number down and right (0 and 1, 2 and 3, ... 46 and 47), so the upper jack takes the even number; the uplinks print 0 to 3 in white between their two lamps. Port numbers are as printed on the metal, from 0. The Junos interface names are not printed: the guide's Table 2 gives PIC 0 as 48x10/100/1000 Base-T and PIC 1 as 4x10G SFP/SFP+, i.e. ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47 and xe-0/1/0 to xe-0/1/3; they are recorded here and not in an interfaces block because the faceplate does not print them. Table 11 notes that on the EX2300-48T only the ports labelled 0/0 through 0/15 and 0/24 through 0/39 support half-duplex.

power.note: Table 14: maximum power consumed by the switch 70 W, no PoE; Table 15: 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 1.2 A at 100 VAC and 0.6 A at 240 VAC.

rear-layout.note: estimated - positions off the 48P rear photograph (3.234 px per mm across, 3.09 px per mm down) for the management and console jacks, USB port, earthing terminal and AC inlet, which Figure 12 shows at the same places on the 48-port non-PoE model. Figure 12 draws the ESD point lower and to the right of the earthing plate and the single exhaust fan at 0.263 of the width (116.2 mm), as the DC rear photograph does, so the ESD symbol and point and the fan take that photograph's positions; no earth symbol is drawn because the DC photograph shows none and no photograph shows this rear. The guide's drawing puts a serial number label and a CLEI label on the rear; the studio photographs show neither, so none is drawn. The five edge screws are read off Figure 12 (the body 874 px across at 1.978 px per mm, the first at 52.1 mm and the last at 386.7 mm, centres, drawn at y 37.4 as on the DC rear) and are estimated; no photograph of this rear is held, and the held NetBox 24T rear elevation shows the 24-port non-PoE rear, which carries nine. The AC legend is drawn from the guide's Table 15 (1.2 A at 100 VAC for this model) and not read off a figure.

sources.note: EX2300 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2025-08-12 (314 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex2300/ex2300.pdf): Figure 3 and Figure 4 (front panels), Figure 9 to Figure 13 (rear panels), Table 1 (models), Table 3 (chassis size and weight), Tables 4 to 12 (LEDs), the cooling system section, Tables 14 to 16 (power) and Table 34 (parts list). Juniper's own straight-on studio photographs of the EX2300-48P front and rear and of the EX2300-24P front. The maker's image library holds no photograph of the EX2300-48T (the address the brief gave returned a page, not an image). The HPE PSNow datasheet (a00151236enw) did not answer when fetched, so no datasheet is cited.

uplinks.note: photo-measured - one row of four SFP+/SFP cages numbered 0 to 3 with a pair of lamp slots flanking each numeral; the guide gives 4x10G SFP/SFP+ and says the ports can be Virtual Chassis ports with SFP+ transceivers but not with SFP.
